items.note: Story 1: Association formed 1889, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891, Gideon Vose first president.
Story 1: by-laws pay by butterfat test not milk weight, station test determines pay. 'Article VII' not named, but no REQUIRED line, so the core rule carries it.
Story 1: the rule 'made the defects that followed financially catastrophic'.
Loomis, Teague and Sill are not named in Section A.
Story 5: Selby Vose, son of Gideon (explicitly not nephew). No year in Section A. The run's 1911 appears only in B3/D3 and is deducted there.
Station-gain ledger line is absent from Section A (mentioned only in C3/D2).
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896. Borrowed Larrow Green glass not mentioned, but the core fact is present.
Story 1 (weigh, sample, test, cream down, skim back) together with Story 8 (short measure into a bottle whose neck is ruled for a full one).
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Never says the shortfall was flat, the same 0.19 in every month. It gives a '0.19-0.21' gap and elsewhere attributes part of it to seasonal hay.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Stories 1, 6 and 7: hired at the 1896 opening, 29 seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, 1861-1934.
Bench routine in Story 1; station test book in Stories 4 and 8. Thin, but both gating elements are there.
Summary leaf missing: 1896 at 3.80 is not given in Section A, only 3.61 'before'.
Story 4: 8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests higher then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the core fact is present.
Stories 5 and 7: wife Orra, brother-in-law Emmet Brant, the largest and most damaged patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but not Keddie's statement that he 'cannot say why the figures are what they are'. 'Tested the way he was taught' is the run's own narration.
Story 7: died 1934 unvindicated. Story 8: records deposited at the County Historical Rooms.
Story 3: Hessel Bottom, wet ground, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the agreement of the two scales are not in Section A.
Conflation gate: states the Hollow-vs-Green or valley gap as '0.19-0.21' (Story 2, C1b, F1), which loses the item.
Says the committee 'sampled herds in every season' instead of Jan-Mar 1908. Elsewhere (F) it asserts the hay as a partial true cause.
Brant's 1910 year and the proportional loss (Vose Jerseys) are not in Section A.
Weigh book passing to Roy Brant, lent to Ivy 1958, then Hazel: not in Section A.
Alder Corners is absent from the entire answer sheet.
Four patrons hauling to Alder Corners from 1915: absent.
Independence of the Alder Corners test: absent.
Same milk about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen seasons: absent.
Same milk tested differently in two buildings: absent.
Rosalie Cudd copying figures for Ivy: absent.
Strawn named as independent state inspector, but his circuit is dated 'from 1908' (NT-23 wrong value), not 1907-1936.
Story 6: lactometer at every visit, never once found added water.
Section A says only 'summer 1923'. The gated date of 12 June is absent (burette and whole-lot condemnation are present).
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency.
Gives the 28 June / 2 July letters, but the 1924 average as 3.85 rather than 3.80.
Story 8: the crate had been in the station loft since the 1923 condemnation.
Story 6: petition January 1925.
Story 6: Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Story 6: watering (manager), theft by the tester (Association officer), bog hay. None sustained.
The four-book exhibit list appears only in F, not in Section A.
Story 6: dismissed 30 April, before any finding. Award 4 May, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
No one-fifth of $19,000 and no link to the gain account. Section A gives a $19,600 loss.
Story 8: Ivy, granddaughter, b.1931, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Never says Ivy assembled records that had never been in the same room.
February 1958, station loft, but 'eleven remained intact' (NT-16) instead of nine.
Gives 16.27 cc, short 1.33 cc, about 7.5% (NT-1), instead of 16.72, 0.88 and 0.95.
No 95-percent-of-true or 3.61-for-3.80 statement. Uses the 7.5% cascade.
Gives 67,000 lb and $19,600. No 40M/76,000/$19,000 and no ledger identity.
Story 8: Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cleared him 24 years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Derivation: Ansel to son Duncan to daughter Ivy.
Second cousins, derived via Orra (Emmet's sister) and first cousins Duncan and Roy.
A08 abstention missing. Never raises full vs half siblings; the 'left open' point is about collaboration instead. No assertion, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, his father.
Significance is given as inherited institutional credibility. There is no Article VII link and no Vose Jerseys point.
A01 asserted: 'There was no family relationship between the Voses and the Keddies.'
Treats Duncan's denial as settling it ('more reliable than rumor'). The key says a family member's denial is not a record.
Gives 16.27/17.6, 7.56% short (NT-1 cascade), not 0.95.
Gives true 3.905 and shortfall 0.30, not 3.80 and 0.19.
Gives 80,000, 120,000 and settles on 67,000 lb, not 76,000.
Gives $16,750 / $19,600 and 19.4%, not $19,000 and one fifth.
Gives 7,400 true and 560 owed, not 7,200 and 360.
Gives 120,000 lb as 8.3% / 7.7%, not 76,000 as 5.00% of delivered and 5.26% of credited.
$77.93 with correct line items.
72 pipettes is right, but shortfall given as 1.33 cc, not 0.88.
Gives 26 years and '21 full years 1902-1923', with a complaint-based reason. Not 26 yr 6 wk vs 25 full years 1898-1922.

A02: says the first-season sheets did not survive and gives Kyle's 1,100,000 only as an 'unreliable', 'uncertain' recollection 'not in any book'. Under the mechanical test this has no unqualified verdict sentence, so it counts as an abstention.
Variable: the measuring glass / pipette; only the glass differed.
Held constant: tester, herds, procedure, machinery, season, pasture.
Only 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'. No 3.80 or 3.61.
Leaves the glass-vs-wet-hay proportion open, so feed is not eliminated. None of the key's limits (cc size, which glass, whose measure) is given.
Only two valid reasons (the 1911 interval, Strawn's lactometer), both attributed to Falke. The third (family structure/motive) is not valid.
Argues independence and names the 1911 interval as holding without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'No.' The bookkeeper did not question it.
Yes: knew the station tested low. Cites the 1919 circular and the recurring complaint.
Only two of five (signed the accounts, 1919 circular). Manager year given as 1911. Neither the hearing argument nor the 'never names glassware' point.
A03 not declined. Asserts 'He was looking for farmer misconduct or land problems, not manufacturing failure.'
Row 13 only: circular to nine families, not eleven, resolved in E. Other E1 entries are not keyed conflicts or are resolved wrongly (67,000/$19,600).
NT-18: great-niece named as carried by two sources and broken by the family record and the closing correction. No other pairs noticed.
A04, A06 and A10 not treated as abstention conflicts in Sections B-G.
Oram's eleven/nine is offered as a self-contradiction, but it is not one of the key's listed self-refutations.
Uses 16.27 and 7.56%, with hay offsetting to 0.19. No 95% or 0.19 = 5% of 3.80. 1924 given as 3.85.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same man at the bench.
Cites Bulletin 214 but half-adopts the decoy: hay 'partially correct', contributing 0.05 of the gap.
A07 asserted: 'No.'
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie suspected it was the glass.'
Summary is well over 150 words (about 270), though it claims 147.
Names the test book, weigh books, inspector's notebooks, Association ledgers, arbitration documents and the 1958 measurement.
Contains 16.27, $19,600 and hay as 'partially true'.
Only three of six elements (1897, 1958, both names). No one-in-twenty, no 76,000/$19,000, and 1923 is not stated.

deductions.reason: Corruption: gap of 0.21 asserted in F ('the observed 0.21-point gap') (F076)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (B3, D3)
Corruption: circular carried to eleven families, asserted in Story 5 (F058)
Corruption: 1908 committee sampled 'in every season', i.e. the whole of 1908 (F096)
Corruption: bog hay asserted as a real partial cause of the gap (F107)
Gullibility: A01 Vose-Keddie kinship asserted 'no relationship' (B4)
Gullibility: A09 bookkeeper never questioned entries asserted (D2)
Gullibility: A03 manager's knowledge of the instrument fault asserted (D3)
Gullibility: A07 board did not examine glassware asserted (F)
Gullibility: A05 tester believed it was the glass asserted (F)
